title: Jasper and Copy.ai alternative: content that actually ships
author: Cryptool
excerpt_html: AI writers hand you a draft. Someone still has to edit it, decide where it goes, publish it, and do the same thing again next week.
content_html:
Jasper and Copy.ai solved the blank page, which was a real problem and is now largely solved everywhere. What they did not solve is the rest of the pipeline. A draft in a text box is not a published post, and the distance between the two is where most content programmes quietly die: someone has to edit it, decide which channel it suits, format it, publish it, and then start again next week without being asked. GTM handles that whole loop, and it comes with your Cryptool account.

What the AI writers do well

They generate usable first drafts fast, in a consistent voice once you have configured one, across a wide range of formats. Jasper has proper brand voice controls and team features. Copy.ai has workflow building and a large template library. If your bottleneck is genuinely the writing, and you have someone to take the output onward, they earn their subscription.

Where it stalls

The output is the input to a process nobody owns. In practice a founder generates a few posts in the first week, publishes two, and the tab stays closed after that. The work that makes content compound is not writing, it is showing up repeatedly, and a generator does not create the discipline to do that.

Scope is the other limit. A copy tool has no view of whether the piece targets a query anyone searches, whether it got published, whether anyone mentioned it afterwards, or whether it connected to a commercial conversation. Those are all separate tools and separate habits.

What GTM does

It publishes, not just drafts. Content is produced on-brand and published across your connected channels, so there is no handoff step waiting on a person.

It targets search deliberately. SEO and search advertising run alongside the content, so what gets written is aimed at being found rather than at filling a calendar.

It tracks mentions. You learn where the project is being discussed, which is the feedback loop a copy generator has no access to.

It links to outreach and sales. Content, outreach and partnership motions sit in the same system, so a piece has somewhere to lead.

It keeps going. The value is continuity. A generator is only as consistent as the person opening it; an always-on system does not need to be remembered.

Choosing between them

If you have a marketer who wants to write faster and keep full editorial control over every piece, an AI writing tool is the better fit, and it should be their tool rather than the whole programme. If you have nobody, and the honest position is that content will otherwise not happen, then the draft was never the missing piece and GTM addresses the actual gap.

Common questions

Is GTM just an AI writer with publishing attached?

Writing and publishing are part of it, alongside SEO, search advertising, mention tracking and support for outreach and sales. The point is the loop rather than any single step in it.

Will the content sound like our project?

You set up your brand first, and the content is produced from that setup. As with any tool of this kind, the quality of the brand setup is what determines the quality of the output.

Do I keep editorial control?

You control the brand configuration and which channels are connected. If you want a person approving every sentence before it publishes, that is a different operating model and an AI writing tool suits it better.

Is GTM free?

It comes with your Cryptool account.
